svg.aria-label: Hydrolysis of sucrose: inversion of rotation
svg.title: Hydrolysis of sucrose: inversion of rotation
svg.text: Hydrolysis of sucrose: inversion of rotation
Because the sign changes from dextro (+) to laevo (–), the hydrolysis is called INVERSION and the product INVERT SUGAR.
Fructose is more strongly laevorotatory than glucose is dextrorotatory, so the mixture is laevorotatory.
Invert sugar is sweeter than sucrose (fructose ≈ 1.7 × sucrose) – the basis of honey and confectionery syrups.
